text:
devon: heads up — noticed a regression on the TP all-reduce path after last kernel-selector tweak. end-to-end latency for 8-GPU TP jobs jumped ~18% on membound workloads. I think tree fallback + small-message fragmentation is serializing the pipeline.
maria: can you paste the top-level perf numbers?
devon: yesterday baseline (ring-pref): 1.0x. after change (tree-prefer for small chunks): 1.18x median latency, tails up to 1.4x.
kevin: ugh. any KV-cache interaction? sometimes KV cache flushes increase short-lived traffic.
devon: yes — KV cache warmups spike the number of tiny allreduces (4–64KB). profiler shows a lot of active CPU time doing handshake/serialize per-chunk instead of overlapping with compute.
nashley: do we have flamegraphs or nccl timeline?
devon: uploaded quick traces: perf-bot: flamegraph: https://perf.infra/fg/3130056789, nvprof timeline: https://perf.infra/timeline/3130056789
perf-bot: new flamegraph and timeline uploaded for thread 3130056789 (:rocket:)
maria: looking at the flame — ~60% of time is stalled waiting on NCCL recv for small messages, and ~25% is short kernel launches. overlap is poor.
kevin: that matches a serialization effect — tree reduces pairwise leads to more synchronization points than the ring for these msg sizes. tree wins at huge sizes but loses at many tiny messages.
nashley: what does kernel selector pick now exactly? small-frag threshold was lowered last week to 16KB and we flipped to tree in that range.
devon: correct. selector.conf snippet: ``` {"small_frag_threshold_bytes":16384, "prefer_tree_for_small":true, "coalesce_window_ms":0.8} ```
maria: coalesce_window is tiny. if KV cache causes many small requests we should try local coalescing before sending to the comm layer. increase coalesce_window or enable prefix batching.
kevin: agree. quick A/B: revert prefer_tree_for_small=false and bump coalesce_window to 3.0ms, run canonical TP-load.
devon: started a run with that config on 8xA100 — regression mostly gone in the 10-minute test: median back to 1.02x, tail down to 1.1x.
nashley: promising. any memory pressure tradeoffs? larger coalesce window can increase peak GPU memory if requests queue up.
devon: measured 3–5% extra GPU memory in our load; still within safety margins. KV cache hit ratio improved slightly because we served more from merged requests.
maria: long-term we should adjust kernel-selector heuristics to be traffic-shape aware (burstiness + KV-cache warmups). maybe add a dynamic probe that picks ring/tree per-window and remembers for a few seconds.
kevin: also worth tuning aggregation in the runtime so we coalesce adjacent KV cache misses on the same TP stage. That reduces the number of distinct allreduces.
nashley: can we add a lightweight sampler that tracks outstanding small reduces per-stage and flips algorithm when > X per second? low overhead counters.
devon: I'll prototype a counter + hysteresis (switch after 50 small-reduces/s sustained for 2s). will run overnight.
perf-bot: scheduled nightly job: tp-allreduce-sampling-probe on 8xA100 at 03:00 UTC (job id 3130056801)
maria: once we have stable probe numbers we can bake heuristics into kernel-selector and coalescing defaults. also add an eval that simulates KV-cache warmup patterns.
kevin: let's also add a metric to console: small_allreduce_rate, avg_coalesce_delay, and per-stage overlap_pct so customers can see if they're hitting this.
devon: created ticket INF-2317 with links to traces + config diffs. I'll post results tomorrow. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
